title: LoRA selected for the final production fit

data.title: LoRA selected for the final production fit
paragraphs: The full-tuning pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 39.8 active training minutes, visiting 69,791 microphone views. Best and final exports are byte-identical and share their decode results. On the unchanged development panel, macro WER is 31.39%, slightly lower than the mixed LoRA reference at 31.70%. This is a 0.31 percentage point reduction and 0.98% relative improvement.

The saved policy rejected promotion to full tuning. The relative gain is below the required 2%, and the paired cluster 95% interval for candidate minus reference spans -2.13 to +1.90 percentage points, including zero. AMI also regresses by 2.011 percentage points, just above the declared two-point per-dataset limit. The evidence does not establish a sufficiently reliable, balanced improvement for this tested full-tuning recipe. It does not establish that full tuning can never help under other budgets or settings; no additional search is authorized in this bounded campaign.

Full tuning improves CHiME 6 WER to 61.21% from 64.06%, Common Voice to 7.68% from 7.82%, and VOiCES to 17.70% from 17.96%. AMI worsens to 38.95% from 36.94%. Quiet-view WER worsens to 50.18% from 47.95%, although it remains within the three-point guard. Both models produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. Those probes do not validate behavior on real background voices or product microphones.

All seven permitted pilots and their development-based decisions are complete. The selected method is mixed LoRA with the original dataset loss weights: Common Voice 40.08%, AMI 31.36%, CHiME 6 18.56%, and VOiCES 10.00%. The production supervisor has automatically launched the single three-pass production_all_audio fit, using the full retained training and development pool with the existing microphone-alignment and quiet-channel safeguards. The final fit starts from the pretrained base under the selected recipe rather than continuing a pilot checkpoint.

At this check, production is in compilation and memory/gradient preflight, with 16 of 22 shapes complete and no production optimizer checkpoint yet. Its planned budget is 517,569 updates, with the declared larger LoRA batch limits of 16 examples, 120 padded audio seconds and 2,048 tokens. These are the existing production settings, not a new experiment. Monitoring remains at 15 minutes through startup; it can back off once production optimizer steps and checkpoints are advancing normally.

Development has now been folded into the final training pool after recipe selection, while frozen final tests remain excluded. The production model has not yet been evaluated, and development scores cannot serve as independent final accuracy evidence. There is no independent final age test or real product-microphone validation, and the screening has no second-seed confirmation. This is a bounded recipe choice, not proof of globally optimal weights or general superiority of LoRA.

At the 24 October 2026 02:36 UTC snapshot, the dashboard estimates approximately 26-45 hours remaining to a production model, including final export. This is a planning range based on the selected LoRA method and earlier throughput; it will be refined after production preflight and measured training progress. It excludes pauses, sleep and unexpected recovery time.
